skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: Equate the total sector area to $90\%$ of the trapezium area using the geometry shown.
Resolve each sloping side: the height is $r\sin x$ and the top base is $CD=2r-2r\cos x$.
The two sectors have total area $r^2x$; use $\frac12(AB+CD)\times r\sin x$ for the trapezium.
Cancel $r^2$ and simplify to the required equation.
walkthrough:
Calculate the combined area of the two shaded circular sectors:
Each sector has radius $r$ and angle $x$ radians, so the area of one sector is $\dfrac{1}{2}r^2 x$.
The sum of the areas of both sectors is:
$$\text{Area of sectors} = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}r^2 x\right) = r^2 x$$

Calculate the area of the trapezium $ABCD$:
The longer base is $AB = 2r$.
The perpendicular height from $D$ to $AB$ is $h = r\sin x$.
The horizontal projection of $AD$ onto $AB$ is $r\cos x$.
Since the trapezium is isosceles, the shorter parallel base is:
$$CD = AB - 2(r\cos x) = 2r - 2r\cos x = 2r(1 - \cos x)$$

Apply the trapezium area formula $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}(AB + CD) \times h$:
$$\text{Area of trapezium} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2r + 2r - 2r\cos x\right)(r\sin x) = \dfrac{1}{2}(4r - 2r\cos x)(r\sin x) = r^2(2 - \cos x)\sin x$$

Equate the sector area to $90\% = 0.9$ of the trapezium area:
$$r^2 x = 0.9\left(r^2(2 - \cos x)\sin x\right)$$

Divide both sides by $r^2$ ($r > 0$):
$$x = 0.9(2 - \cos x)\sin x$$
This completes the proof.

ai_rubric.Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regi: Identifies $CD=2r-2r\cos x$; Applies a formula for the area of a sector and trapezium, or equivalent, form an equation in $r$ and $x$; Derives $x=0.9(2-\cos x)\sin x$.

hints: Form a continuous residual from the equation and test it at both stated endpoints in radians.
For example evaluate $g(x)=0.9(2-\cos x)\sin x-x$ at $0.5$ and $0.7$.
Show the two values have opposite signs, then conclude that a root lies between them.
walkthrough: Define the continuous function $g(x) = 0.9(2 - \cos x)\sin x - x$.

Conclude using the intermediate value theorem:
Since $g(0.5) < 0$ and $g(0.7) > 0$, there is a sign change across the interval $[0.5, 0.7]$. By the intermediate value theorem, the root $x$ lies strictly between $0.5$ and $0.7$.

ai_rubric.Numerical Root Bracketing: Endpoint evaluations at 0.5 and 0.7 establish the sign change or ordering. Completes the argument with values. The diagram or calculation gives a sign change occurs between $x=0.5$ and $x=0.7$.

hints: At convergence, consecutive terms approach the same limit; call that common value $x$.
Replace both $x_{n+1}$ and $x_n$ in the iteration by $x$, then take cosine of both sides.
Rearrange $\cos x=2-x/(0.9\sin x)$ to recover exactly the root equation from part (a).
walkthrough:
Assume the sequence $x_{n+1} = \cos^{-1}\!\left(2 - \dfrac{x_n}{0.9\sin x_n}\right)$ converges to a limit $L$ in $0 < L < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:
$$L = \lim_{n\to\infty} x_{n+1} = \lim_{n\to\infty} x_n$$

Taking the limit on both sides of the recurrence relation gives:
$$L = \cos^{-1}\!\left(2 - \dfrac{L}{0.9\sin L}\right)$$

Apply the cosine function to both sides:
$$\cos L = 2 - \dfrac{L}{0.9\sin L}$$

Rearrange to isolate $L$:
$$\dfrac{L}{0.9\sin L} = 2 - \cos L$$
$$L = 0.9(2 - \cos L)\sin L$$

State the conclusion:
This equation in $L$ is identical to $x = 0.9(2 - \cos x)\sin x$ from part (a), confirming that the sequence converges to the root of the original equation.

ai_rubric.Fixed-Point Iteration: Gives a displayed equation, e.g. $\cos x=2-\frac{x}{0.9\sin x}$. Rearranges to $x=0.9\sin x(2-\cos x)$. At convergence, $x=\cos^{-1}(2-x/(0.9\sin x))$ rearranges to $x=0.9(2-\cos x)\sin x$.

hints: Apply the supplied fixed-point formula in radian mode, starting with a value in $0.5<x<0.7$.
Use each displayed result as the next $x_n$ and record every iterate to 4 decimal places.
Continue until the iterates justify a single value to 2 decimal places; do not round the internal calculation prematurely.
walkthrough:
Use the iterative formula $x_{n+1} = \cos^{-1}\!\left(2 - \dfrac{x_n}{0.9\sin x_n}\right)$ with an initial value within the bracket, for example $x_1 = 0.6$:
$$x_2 = \cos^{-1}\!\left(2 - \dfrac{0.6}{0.9\sin(0.6)}\right) \approx 0.5843$$
$$x_3 = \cos^{-1}\!\left(2 - \dfrac{0.5843}{0.9\sin(0.5843)}\right) \approx 0.5748$$
$$x_4 = \cos^{-1}\!\left(2 - \dfrac{0.5748}{0.9\sin(0.5748)}\right) \approx 0.5690$$
$$x_5 = \cos^{-1}\!\left(2 - \dfrac{0.5690}{0.9\sin(0.5690)}\right) \approx 0.5654$$
$$x_6 = \cos^{-1}\!\left(2 - \dfrac{0.5654}{0.9\sin(0.5654)}\right) \approx 0.5632$$
$$x_7 = \cos^{-1}\!\left(2 - \dfrac{0.5632}{0.9\sin(0.5632)}\right) \approx 0.5618$$
$$x_8 = \cos^{-1}\!\left(2 - \dfrac{0.5618}{0.9\sin(0.5618)}\right) \approx 0.5610$$

Observe that the iterations stabilize and round to $0.56$ to 2 decimal places.
(Checking interval $(0.555, 0.565)$: $g(0.555) < 0$ and $g(0.565) > 0$, confirming rounding.)
Thus:
$$x = 0.56$$

ai_rubric.Fixed-Point Iteration: Substitution into $x$ gives consecutive iterates $0.62\to0.615\to0.625$, converging to $x=0.62$.
